_meta.scope: pod-0 flagged units from services/pod-lego-extractor.cjs dry runs (hrv_for_eng 57, gle_for_eng 43)
_meta.doctrine: ZUT >= understandable > minimal-vocab > maximal-pattern > naturalness; literal nuance -> note, never competing gloss; particles glue; identity chunks passthrough; canonical must hold in every occurrence
_meta.split_into: for verdict=split, the two defined units; the entry's own canonical_known is the primary sense (keeps the original lego_key)

dobro.note: dobro is also the adverb 'well' — govoriš dobro = you speak well
dobro.rationale: 6/8 occurrences are 'good' (greetings); the 2 adverbial uses read understandably as 'good' with the note carrying the adverb reading.

da.rationale: Genuine homograph: standalone answer 'yes' (10 occ) vs complementizer 'that' (4 occ: nadam se da, moguće da, čini se da); no single gloss holds.

split_into.when: complementizer linking clauses; prefer gluing to the following clause per the particle rule when re-tiling lands

dan.note: Dobar dan (lit. 'good day') is the standard daytime greeting — English 'good afternoon'
dan.rationale: 'afternoon' (1 occ) is the greeting's English rendering, not the word's meaning; 'day' holds everywhere with the greeting note.

je-li.rationale: Question form of je; 'is...?' holds in all 3 occurrences and partitions against je = 'is' (ZUT); 'is it that' was a decorated literal.

ne.rationale: Answer-word 'no' vs verbal negator 'not' (ako ne budemo = if we won't be); negator is a particle that should glue to its verb.

split_into.when: verbal negator; prefer gluing to the verb ('ne budemo' = 'we won't be')

molim.note: molim is literally 'I ask' — the all-purpose Croatian 'please'
molim.rationale: 13/14 glosses are 'please'; the one decorated gloss baked the literal into the text — the literal belongs in the first-encounter note.

izvolite.note: izvolite is the all-purpose service/invitation word — handing something over, ushering someone, or 'go ahead'
izvolite.rationale: Four different glosses, all the same service-word; 'here you go' matches the unflagged informal izvoli and holds (with the note) in all 4 contexts.

što.rationale: Interrogative 'what' (5 occ) vs complementizer 'that' after emotion predicates (sretan što = happy that, 1 occ); no single gloss holds.

split_into.when: complementizer after feeling-words; prefer gluing to the preceding predicate when re-tiling lands

mogu.rationale: Same form glossed 3 ways (incl. both orders for the identical sentence 'Što mogu donijeti?'); 'I can' is the form's identity and frees 'can I' for mogu li (fixes a live ZUT collision).

donijeti.rationale: 'bring it' (1 occ) just folded in an English-required object; 'bring' holds in all 4.

želim.rationale: Verified collision: željela bih is already canonically 'I'd like'; želim is literally 'I want' and holds in all 3 occurrences (ZUT outranks politeness-naturalness).

kavu.rationale: Bare noun is the only gloss that holds both standalone ('a coffee') and inside 'crnu kavu' ('black coffee'); articles are sentence packaging.

puno.rationale: 'a lot' holds everywhere — 'thanks a lot' (hvala puno) and 'a lot of traffic' (puno prometa); 'very much' fails the quantity use.

doviđenja.rationale: Current canonical has the literal baked into the gloss text; gloss = 'goodbye', literal = first-encounter note.

možemo-li.rationale: 'could we' (2 occ) is English politeness drift on the same Croatian form; 'can we' holds everywhere.

oprosti.rationale: 'sorry' holds in both occurrences (attention-getting and apology) and partitions the T/V register: oprosti = 'sorry', oprostite stays 'excuse me' (reduces a 3-way 'excuse me' collision).

drago-mi-je.note: said on its own when meeting someone = 'pleased to meet you' (lit. 'it is dear to me')
drago-mi-je.rationale: 'pleased to meet you' fails in 'drago mi je što smo se upoznali' (= pleased THAT we met); 'I'm pleased' holds in both with the greeting note.

ja-sam.rationale: 'I'm' (1 occ) is contraction drift only; majority canonical holds everywhere.

to.rationale: 'it' (1 occ) is English rendering drift; demonstrative 'that' is understandable in both occurrences.

malo.rationale: 'a little' holds in all 5 (a little slower / a little cider / a little bread / take a little / a little frustrating); the alternates were sentence-side renderings.

to-je.rationale: 'that's' holds in all 3 occurrences ('that's near here / that's very kind / that's twelve euros'); current canonical 'it's' fails two of them.

želiš-li.rationale: 'would you like' (1 occ) is politeness drift; 'do you want' is the form's identity and holds in both.

malu.rationale: 'regular' was barista-English from one sentence's rendering; 'small' is the word and holds in both (ZUT outranks menu-naturalness).

mogu-li-dobiti.rationale: Composes with the sibling units mogu li = 'can I' + dobiti = 'get'; holds understandably in both occurrences.

i.rationale: Genuine polysemy: conjunction 'and' (11 occ) vs additive focus particle (3 occ: i čašu vode = a glass of water AS WELL); no single gloss holds. 'as well' (not 'also') keeps ZUT against također = 'also'.

split_into.when: additive particle directly before the added thing

odmah.rationale: Temporal 'right away' (2 occ) vs spatial intensifier (odmah iza ugla = right round the corner, 1 occ); 'right away' cannot hold spatially. 'right' (not 'just') keeps ZUT against samo = 'just'.

split_into.when: intensifier before a location; prefer gluing to the locative ('odmah iza ugla' = 'right round the corner')

još.rationale: 'another' holds in both ('another two glasses', 'another something') and avoids colliding with više = 'more'; the s#35 glosses had još/nešto crossed.

nešto.rationale: 'else' was a crossed gloss (it belongs to još in 'još nešto'); 'something' is the word and holds in all 3.

mogu-li.rationale: 'could I' (1 occ) is politeness drift; 'can I' holds everywhere (and mogu is remapped to 'I can', clearing the collision).

dobiti.rationale: Both occurrences follow a modal (mogu li / možemo li …); bare 'get' composes with 'can I' and matches mogu-li-dobiti = 'can I get'.

čašu.rationale: Every occurrence precedes a genitive (vode/piva/vina); carrying the 'of' on the container word matches the unflagged čaše = 'glasses of' convention and holds in all 5.

vode.rationale: Bare 'water' holds everywhere; the 'of' belongs to the container unit (čašu/bocu).

imate-li.note: the -te ending (imate, možete…) is the polite/plural 'you' — used to strangers throughout these scenes
imate-li.rationale: The alternate was the same gloss with '— politely' decoration; the register fact belongs in one first-encounter note, not in gloss text.

piva.rationale: One surface covers gen.sg ('of beer') and nom.pl ('beers'); bare 'beer' is the only gloss that holds in all 3 — case/number is carried by context.

vidjeti.rationale: All 3 occurrences follow a modal; bare 'see' composes ('can I see').

vinsku-kartu.rationale: 'the wine list' (1 occ) is article drift; 'wine list' holds in both.

vina.rationale: Bare 'wine' is the only gloss holding all 4 (gen.sg 'of wine' ×2, 'white/red wine', pl. 'our wines'); 'of' lives on čašu = 'a glass of'.

možete.rationale: Strip the '— politely' decoration (register lives in the imate-li note); 'you can' holds in both occurrences.

evo.rationale: Neither 'here are' nor 'here is' holds in both occurrences (plural menus vs singular passport); colloquial 'here's' covers both.

bez-glutena.rationale: Both known texts say 'gluten-free'; the transparent literal becomes the first-encounter note.

ima-li.note: ima li is literally 'has it / is there' — with a subject it asks 'does X have' (Ima li soba pogled? = Does the room have a view?)
ima-li.rationale: Existential 'is there' is the majority (2/3) and the possessive reading (1 occ) is the same Croatian construction — one gloss + note beats splitting a single deviant occurrence.

protiv-bolova.note: literally 'against pain' — lijekovi protiv bolova = painkillers
protiv-bolova.rationale: English idiom is medicine FOR pain; the literal 'against' reading is a note, not a competing gloss.

s-lijeve-strane.rationale: 'on your left' (1 occ) is rendering drift; 'on the left' holds in both.

trebam.rationale: 'should I' (1 occ) was the question-rendering of 'how often do I need to…'; 'I need' holds understandably in all 3.

kupiti.rationale: Bare 'buy' is the only form composing after both governors (trebam kupiti = need to buy; mogu kupiti = can buy); English 'to' is junction glue.

bili-ste.rationale: Alternate was the same gloss with '— politely' decoration; strip it (register covered by the imate-li note).

mi.rationale: Dative clitic; 'to me' holds in both occurrences ('been of great help to me', 'recommend something to me').

od-velike-pomoći.rationale: Both known texts render it 'very helpful'; the literal is already captured in the chunk's literal field and becomes the note.

vježbati.rationale: Three spellings/forms of one verb; bare UK 'practise' matches the corpus's majority spelling and composes after trebam/moram/nastaviti.

podne.rationale: 'midday' is the word's meaning and holds in 'do podne' (until midday); 'afternoon' was the greeting's rendering — see TOM-CALL on the greeting text itself.

odlično.rationale: Three glosses for one exclamation; 'wonderful' holds in all 3 and avoids piling onto the existing 'excellent' (odličan/izvrsna) and 'lovely' (divan/divna) collisions.

soba.rationale: Bare 'room' is the only gloss holding all 3 occurrences, including the apposition 'soba sedam nula devet' (room 709).

možete-li.rationale: Strip decoration, plain 'can you' — completes the can-paradigm (mogu = I can, mogu li = can I, možemo li = can we, možete = you can).

glavobolju.rationale: 'a headache' holds in both ('I have a headache', 'paracetamol for a headache'); 'the' was rendering drift.

ima.rationale: 'there is' (1 occ) is contraction drift; 'there's' holds in both and stays distinct from ima li = 'is there'.

možda.rationale: 'perhaps' is a pure synonym; one canonical, 'maybe' (majority/first-seen) holds everywhere.

točno.rationale: 'exactly' holds in both ('drop you exactly by the ticket office', 'exactly the kind of practice'); 'right' fails the second.

go-raibh-maith-agat.note: a fixed expression — literally 'may there be good at you'
go-raibh-maith-agat.rationale: Fixed expression stays whole; the decorated alternates baked teaching commentary into gloss text — that's the first-encounter note's job.

an-bhfuil.note: the question form of tá ('is/are') — Irish has no verb 'to have': an bhfuil … agat (lit. 'is … at you') asks 'do you have …?'
an-bhfuil.rationale: 8 alternates all collapse to 'question-form of be'; the have-readings come from the agat/agaibh junction; 'is...?' holds everywhere and partitions against tá = 'is'.

tá.rationale: Two genuine functions: declarative 'is' (11 occ; possession/have readings come from the at-pronoun junction) vs sentence-initial echo-answer 'yes' (7 occ); no single gloss holds.

split_into.when: standalone echo-answer opening a reply; note: Irish answers 'yes' by repeating the verb — 'yes (it is)' keeps it distinct from sea/bhí

agam.note: tá X agam (lit. 'X is at me') = 'I have X'
agam.rationale: 'I have' fails 'Beidh an t-uan agam' (I'LL have) and 'curtha in áirithe agam' (booked BY me); literal 'at me' is the only gloss holding all 4, with the have-construction as the note.

agat.note: tá X agat (lit. 'X is at you') = 'you have X'
agat.rationale: 6 alternates; literal 'at you' holds in all 11 occurrences and makes the prepositional-pronoun paradigm consistent (at me / at you / at us / at you-plural).

feicfidh-mé.rationale: 'I'll see' is contraction drift; one canonical suffices.

seo.note: sentence-initial Seo X (lit. 'this [is] X') = 'here is X / here are X'
seo.rationale: Demonstrative 'this' holds in both; the presentational use (Seo na biachláir) is the same word doing 'here is' — a note, not a second gloss.

níl.note: literally 'is not' — Irish answers 'no' by negating the verb
níl.rationale: Both occurrences are echo-answers; 'no, it's not' fails s#12 ('No, I'm sorry…'); plain 'no' + the echo-system note holds everywhere.

duit.rationale: 'to you' (1 occ) is the same preposition do; 'for you' holds in all 4 (get for you ×3, slowly enough for you).

ba-mhaith-liom.rationale: 'I would like' (1 occ) is contraction drift only.

caife.rationale: Bare noun holds both standalone and inside 'caife dubh' (black coffee); article is sentence packaging.

dia-duit.note: literally 'God to you' — the standard Irish greeting
dia-duit.rationale: Two of the four glosses baked commentary/literal into the gloss text; gloss = 'hello', literal = note.

labhairt.rationale: One verbal noun, three renderings; bare 'speak' holds after féidir/mian in all 3 and partitions cleanly against ag caint = 'talking'.

an-féidir-linn.rationale: 'is it possible for us' (1 occ) is the literal; 'can we' holds in both and partitions against an bhféadfaimis = 'could we'.

ansin.rationale: Genuine polysemy: temporal 'then' (2 occ) vs spatial 'there' (síos ansin = down there, 1 occ); neither holds for the other.

oíche-mhaith.note: oíche mhaith covers both the evening greeting and the parting 'good night'
oíche-mhaith.rationale: One fixed expression, two English renderings by situation; neither holds everywhere, and splitting one expression into two teach-units would be worse — canonical = majority (2/3) + note.

dom.note: is ainm dom = 'is my name', lit. 'is a name to me'
dom.rationale: 'my' was the rendering of the name idiom only; 'to me' holds in both occurrences and pairs with duit.

freisin.rationale: also/as well/too are pure synonyms; majority canonical 'too' holds in all 5.

is-as.note: Is as X mé = 'I'm from X' — lit. 'is from X me'; the person comes last
is-as.rationale: 'I'm from' folded the trailing mé into the gloss; 'is from' is the chunk's own content, with the word-order quirk as the note.

mé.rationale: All 3 bare-mé occurrences are copula-final (Is as X mé) or object (mé a thabhairt = take me) where 'me' is the honest gloss; subject uses live inside tá mé / níl mé units.

agus-tusa.rationale: Alternate differs only by the question mark.

díreach.rationale: Intensifier 'right (by/round)' (2 occ) vs direction 'straight' with a motion verb (1 occ); a single gloss risks 'go right' being heard as a turn instruction.

split_into.when: intensifier before a location ('right round the corner', 'right by the ticket office')
direction of motion (Téigh díreach = go straight)

é-sin.rationale: 'that is' (1 occ) folded the copula in; 'that' is the chunk's content and holds in both.

tá-sé.rationale: 'it's' is contraction drift; one canonical suffices.

le.rationale: 'to' (1 occ) comes from the réidh le + verbal-noun junction ('ready to'); the preposition's own meaning 'with' holds in the other 4 and is understandable there.

an-bhfuil-tú.rationale: 'do you' (s#30) was the rendering of 'an bhfuil tú ag iarraidh' = lit. 'are you wanting'; 'are you' is the chunk's own content and holds in both.

an-bhféadfainn.rationale: Alternate was the same gloss with 'politely' decoration; strip it.

a-fháil.rationale: 'to have' readings are English service-register drift on the same verbal noun (faigh = get); 'to get' holds in all 8.

sin.rationale: Presentational 'Sin X' = 'that's X' (1 occ) vs postposed determiner 'an séipéal sin' = 'that church' (1 occ); the determiner is glue, not a standalone unit.

split_into.when: sentence-initial presentational (Sin ocht euro caoga = that's eight euros fifty)
after a noun; prefer gluing to its noun per the particle rule ('an séipéal sin' = 'that church')

ar-fad.rationale: 'completely' (1 occ) is intensity drift; 'altogether' holds (loosely but understandably) in all 4.

atá.rationale: atá is the relative form of tá; 'that is' holds in both occurrences ('the ales that-are at you', 'it's you that-is kind') where 'are' fails the second.

againn.note: tá X againn (lit. 'X is at us') = 'we have X'
againn.rationale: Paradigm consistency with agam/agat; literal 'at us' holds in all 4 with the have-construction as the note.

seo-é.rationale: 'here is' (1 occ) is rendering drift on 'Seo é mo phas' (lit. 'here it-is my passport'); 'here it is' holds in both.

an-bhféadfaimis.rationale: 'can we' (1 occ) is drift; 'could we' holds and partitions against an féidir linn = 'can we'.

agaibh.rationale: Consistent with the remapped at-paradigm (agam/agat/againn); 'you have' (1 occ) is the junction reading.

ceart-go-leor.rationale: 'all right' is a spelling variant; one canonical.

go-bhfuil.rationale: 3/4 occurrences are 'go bhfuil tú' = 'that you are'; the elliptical 'Sílim go bhfuil' (= I think so) reads acceptably under the same gloss.

bhí-tú.rationale: 'you've been' is contraction drift; one canonical.

a-dhéanamh.rationale: 'to have (a conversation / a check-out)' is the English idiom for the same Irish 'do/make'; literal 'to do' holds understandably in all 3.

go-dtí.rationale: Core meaning 'to/toward' holds in all 4 — spatial ('to the station') and temporal ('from half seven to ten', 'stay to midday'); 'until' fails the spatial uses.

ag-caint.rationale: 'speaking' (1 occ) is drift; 'talking' holds in all 4 and partitions against labhairt = 'speak'.

bíonn-sé.note: bíonn is the habitual 'is' — for repeated/general states, vs tá for right now
bíonn-sé.rationale: 'it is' erases the habitual and collides with tá sé; 'it tends to be' holds in both occurrences and preserves the distinction.
